scope: Ground fan-out for loose GND pads, then the remaining slow-digital nets. Copper only; no parts moved.

rules: via lands inside the adjacent ground plane fill (In1 for F, In6 for B), 0.35 mm in from its edge
at least 0.15 mm off its own pad, within 0.9 mm (1.6 mm for four ec decoupling caps)
no via under the body of a chip with an exposed pad, except inside the exposed ground pad
no via inside another part's escape ring

rules_added: escape rings: 0.7 mm around pads of fine-pitch parts reserved for their own nets
no tracks inside the pin ring or vias under the body of chips with an exposed pad
soft costs added and capped at 6x instead of multiplied
special-attention signal nets keep their direct path open
vias in another part's courtyard cost more
footprint rule areas (FPC102/FPC103 shell exclusions, J4/J902 via keep-outs, MK430) respected
special pads that lost every via spot within 1.5 mm got a reserved spot and the slow nets were rerouted (71 reservations)

checks.drc_note: against the board before this pass, both refilled with the project rules beside the board file

placement_exports.note: regenerated; only the source board hash changed

checks.via_net_audit: all 917 new vias keep their nets after refill

still_open: 102 slow-group connections, mostly pins walled in by parts placed right in front of fine-pitch rows (U901, U4, FPC102, FPC103, U44)
power rails other than ground (In4 power map)
high-speed pairs and other special-attention nets
limitations: 333 track pieces under 0.15 mm, mostly one-cell jogs at vias and pads
ground stubs are straight at any angle, not on 45 degree lines
16 slow nets are more than twice their shortest length; some use up to 20 vias

router_changes: start from existing vias wired to a cluster
exact via spots within 1.5 mm of own pads
fan-out under QFP bodies (no exposed pad)
